questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You need to create a mail-enabled contact.  
  
Which portal should you use?
questions.explanation:
Mail-enabled contacts are Exchange Online recipient objects and are created in the Exchange admin center under **Recipients** > **Contacts**.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage mail contacts in Exchange Online](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/exchange/recipients-in-exchange-online/manage-mail-contacts)

questions.domain: Manage compliance by using Microsoft Purview
questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You need to create a mail-enabled contact.  
  
Which portal should you use?
questions.explanation:
The Security Administrator role grants access to Microsoft Entra ID Protection, including its reports and risky-user information. Compliance Administrator, Service Administrator, and User Administrator do not provide the required Identity Protection report access. Security Reader would be a more narrowly scoped read-only role, but it is not one of the available choices.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra built-in roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference)

questions.domain: Implement and manage Microsoft Entra identity and access
questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes users with the following device types:  
  
- Windows 10  
- Android  
- iOS  
  
To which devices can Endpoint DLP policies be applied?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP protects and monitors sensitive items on onboarded Windows endpoints; Android and iOS devices are not supported Endpoint DLP platforms. Therefore, only the Windows 10 devices qualify.\
\
**Learn more:** [Learn about Endpoint data loss prevention](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/endpoint-dlp-learn-about)

questions.domain: Manage compliance by using Microsoft Purview
questions.question:
You must notify the human resources department manager whenever a user in that department shares a file or folder from the department’s Microsoft SharePoint site.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the SharePoint site, create an alert.
From the Microsoft Defender portal, create an alert policy.
From the SharePoint admin center, modify the sharing settings
From the Microsoft 365 admin center, configure SharePoint.org settings.

questions.explanation:
A Microsoft Defender alert policy can monitor a SharePoint file or folder sharing activity, limit the policy to the applicable users and site, and send email notifications to the designated manager when the policy conditions are met.\
\
**Learn more:** [Alert policies in the Microsoft Defender portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/alert-policies) · [Audit log activities](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/audit-log-activities)

questions.domain: Manage compliance by using Microsoft Purview
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Office 365.  
  
You notice that email recipients are notified only several days after an incoming email message is identified as spam and quarantined.  
  
You need to ensure that the email recipients receive notification within 24 hours.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Modify the default inbound anti-spam policy.
Modify the global settings for quarantine policies.

questions.explanation:
Global quarantine policy settings control the end-user spam-notification frequency. Setting that frequency to Daily ensures recipients receive quarantine notifications within 24 hours; the available frequencies include every four hours, daily, and weekly.

**Learn more:** [Quarantine notifications in Microsoft 365 - Microsoft Defender for Office 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/quarantine-quarantine-notifications) · [Quarantine policies - Microsoft Defender for Office 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/quarantine-policies)

questions.domain: Implement and manage Microsoft Entra identity and access

options.text: Join the computers to Azure AD.
Create a conditional access policy in Azure AD.
Modify the Intranet zone settings by using Group Policy.
Deploy an Azure AD Connect staging server.

questions.explanation:
Seamless SSO requires browsers to treat the Microsoft Entra automatic sign-in endpoint as part of the Local Intranet zone so they can send the required Kerberos ticket. This setting is deployed to users through Group Policy by configuring the Intranet zone settings.

**Learn more:** [Quickstart: Microsoft Entra seamless single sign-on](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/how-to-connect-sso-quick-start)

You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You create a Conditional Access policy that blocks access to an app named App1 when users trigger a high-risk sign-in event.  
  
You need to reduce impossible-travel false positives when users sign in from the corporate network.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
Configure named locations for the corporate network’s IP ranges. Sign-ins from named locations marked trusted or known improve Microsoft Entra ID Protection’s location-based risk calculations and reduce false positives for risk detections such as impossible travel.

**Learn more:** [Plan a Microsoft Entra ID Protection deployment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-protection/how-to-deploy-identity-protection) · [Microsoft Entra ID Protection to Detect Protected Resource Risks](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/architecture/id-protection-guide-detect)

questions.domain: Implement and manage Microsoft Entra identity and access
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],**Overview**  
  
Fabrikam, Inc. is an electronics company that manufactures consumer products. Fabrikam has 10,000 employees worldwide.  
  
Fabrikam has its main office in London and branch offices in major cities across Europe, Asia, and the United States.  
  
**Existing Environment**  
  
**Active Directory Environment**  
  
The network has an Active Directory forest named fabrikam.com. The forest includes all identities used for user and computer authentication. Each department is represented by a top-level organizational unit (OU) that includes several child OUs for user accounts and computer accounts.  
  
All users authenticate to on-premises applications by signing in to their device using a UPN format of [email protected].  
  
Fabrikam does **NOT** plan to implement identity federation.  
  
**Network Infrastructure**  
  
Each office has a high-speed Internet connection.  
  
Each office contains two domain controllers. Every domain controller is configured as a DNS server.  
  
The public fabrikam.com zone is managed by an external DNS server.  
  
All users connect to an on-premises Microsoft Exchange Server 2016 organization. Users access email by using Outlook Anywhere, Outlook on the web, or the Microsoft Outlook app for iOS. All Exchange servers have the latest cumulative updates installed.  
  
All shared company documents are stored on a Microsoft SharePoint Server farm.  
  
**Requirements**  
  
**Planned Changes**  
  
Fabrikam plans to implement a Microsoft 365 Enterprise subscription and migrate all email and shared documents to the subscription.  
  
Fabrikam plans to implement two pilot projects:  
  
- Project1: During Project1, the mailboxes of 100 users in the sales department will be moved to Microsoft 365.  
- Project2: After Project1 is completed successfully, Microsoft Teams will be enabled in Microsoft 365 for the sales department users.  
  
Fabrikam plans to create a group named UserLicenses to manage allocation of all Microsoft 365 bulk licenses.  
  
**Technical Requirements**  
  
Fabrikam identifies the following technical requirements:  
  
- During Project1, all users must be able to exchange email messages successfully by using their current email address.  
- Users must be able to authenticate to cloud services if Active Directory becomes unavailable.  
- A user named User1 must be able to view all DLP reports from the Microsoft Purview compliance portal.  
- Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise applications must be installed only from a network share.  
- Disruptions to email access must be minimized.  
  
**Application Requirements**  
  
Fabrikam identifies the following application requirements:  
  
- An on-premises web application named App1 must enable users to complete expense reports online. App1 must be available to users from the My Apps portal.  
- Installation of feature updates for Microsoft 365 Apps for enterprise must be minimized.  
  
**Security Requirements**  
  
Fabrikam identifies the following security requirements:  
  
- After the planned migration to Microsoft 365, all users must continue to authenticate to their mailbox and SharePoint sites by using their UPN.  
- Membership of the UserLicenses group must be validated monthly. Unused user accounts must be removed from the group automatically.  
- After the planned migration to Microsoft 365, all users must be signed in automatically to on-premises and cloud-based applications.  
- The principle of least privilege must be used.  
  
You need to ensure that all sales department users can authenticate successfully during Project1 and Project2.  
  
Which authentication strategy should be implemented for the pilot projects?

options.text: password hash synchronization and seamless SSO

questions.explanation:
Password hash synchronization enables cloud authentication using synchronized password hashes and does not depend on on-premises identity components when processing sign-ins, so cloud access remains available if Active Directory is unavailable. Microsoft Entra seamless SSO automatically signs users in to cloud applications from corporate domain-joined devices. Together, they satisfy both resiliency and automatic cloud sign-in requirements.

**Learn more:** [Build more resilient hybrid authentication in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/architecture/resilience-in-hybrid) · [Microsoft Entra seamless single sign-on](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/how-to-connect-sso)

questions.question:
You are assessing the processes required for Project1.  
  
You need to recommend the DNS record that must be created when adding a domain name for the project.  
  
Which DNS record should you recommend?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft 365 verifies ownership of a custom domain by locating the verification value published in a DNS TXT record. This record proves control of the domain without changing existing mail routing, which supports the requirement to minimize email disruption during the pilot migration.\
\
**Learn more:** [Add a custom domain to Microsoft 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/setup/add-domain?view=o365-worldwide) · [External Domain Name System records for Microsoft 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/enterprise/external-domain-name-system-records?view=o365-worldwide)

You are testing a data loss prevention (DLP) policy that protects the sharing of credit card information with external users.  
  
During testing, you find that a user can share credit card information with external users through email. However, the user is blocked from sharing files containing credit card information through Microsoft SharePoint.  
  
You need to prevent the user from sharing credit card information by using both email and SharePoint.  
  
What should you configure?

options.text: the locations of the DLP policy
the conditions of the DLP policy rule
the user overrides of the DLP policy rule
the status of the DLP policy

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Purview DLP policies are scoped by location. To enforce the policy for both email and SharePoint content, the policy must include the Exchange email and SharePoint locations. The existing SharePoint block indicates that the rule is already effective there; adding the email location extends the policy’s enforcement to email.

**Learn more:** [Create and deploy a data loss prevention policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/dlp-create-deploy-policy)

You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription linked to an Azure AD tenant named contoso.com.  
  
You purchase 100 Microsoft 365 Business Voice add-on licenses.  
  
You need to make sure that members of a group named Voice are automatically assigned a Microsoft 365 Business Voice add-on license.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From the Licenses page of the Microsoft 365 admin center, assign the licenses.
From the Microsoft Entra admin center, modify the settings of the Voice group.
From the Microsoft 365 admin center, modify the settings of the Voice group.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft 365 group-based licensing assigns a selected subscription’s licenses to every member of the assigned group, including members added later. In the Microsoft 365 admin center, this is configured from **Billing > Licenses** by selecting the product and assigning it to the group; ordinary group-setting changes do not configure the license assignment.

**Learn more:** [Assign or unassign licenses to a group in the Microsoft 365 admin center](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/manage/manage-group-licenses?view=o365-worldwide)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that includes a user named User1.  
  
You must ensure that User1 can collect and summarize a custom set of data from signals in the Microsoft Defender XDR environment. The solution must **not** require User1 to know KQL.  
  
What should you do in Microsoft Defender XDR?

options.text: From Advanced hunting, create a new query in the query editor.
From Cloud Discovery, create a report.
From API Explorer, create a query.
From Advanced hunting, create a new query in the query builder.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender XDR Advanced hunting guided mode uses the query builder to create queries through selectable data domains, filters, and conditions without requiring Kusto Query Language (KQL). The query editor is the advanced mode and requires KQL knowledge.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an on-premises server named Server1 that is running Windows Server.  
  
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription and use Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps.  
  
You plan to configure Cloud Discovery and enable automatic log upload.  
  
You need to ensure that the log collector can run on Server1.  
  
What should you install on Server1?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps deploys the on-premises Cloud Discovery log collector for automatic log upload on Windows as a Docker container. Docker is therefore required on the server that hosts the collector.

**Learn more:** [Configure automatic log upload using on-premises Docker on Windows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/discovery-docker-windows) · [Configure automatic log upload for continuous reports](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/discovery-docker)

You plan to onboard the devices to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. The devices will connect to Defender for Endpoint through a proxy service.  
  
You need to ensure that the devices use consolidated URLs and static IP ranges when they connect to Defender for Endpoint.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription containing an Azure AD tenant named contoso.com. The tenant includes a user named User1.  
  
You enable Azure AD Identity Protection.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can review the list of users flagged as risky in Azure AD Identity Protection. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege.

You create a sensitivity label named Label1.  
  
To which resource can you apply Label1?
questions.explanation:
Sensitivity labels for containers can be applied to Microsoft 365 groups and SharePoint sites; distribution groups are not supported containers for these labels. Thus, the supported resources are Group1 and Site1, a combination not present in the choices. In the historical behavior reflected by the likely exam item, only the Microsoft 365 group was supported.

**Learn more:** [Use sensitivity labels to protect collaborative workspaces (groups and sites)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/purview/sensitivity-labels-teams-groups-sites) · [Assign sensitivity labels to Microsoft 365 groups in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/users/groups-assign-sensitivity-labels)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has on-premises servers and an Azure AD tenant.  
  
Several months ago, the Azure AD Connect Health agent was installed on every server.  
  
You regularly review the health status for all servers.  
  
Recently, when you tried to view the health status of a server named Server1, you found that Server1 is **not** listed in the Azure AD Connect Servers list.  
  
You suspect that another administrator removed Server1 from the list.  
  
You need to ensure that you can view Server1's health status.  
  
What are two possible ways to achieve this goal? Each correct answer provides a complete solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: From Windows PowerShell, run the Register-AzureADConnectHealthSyncAgent cmdlet.
From Azure Cloud shell, run the Connect-AzureAD cmdlet.
From Server1, reinstall the Azure AD Connect Health agent.
From Server1, change the Azure AD Connect Health services Startup type to Automatic.
From Server1, change the Azure AD Connect Health services Startup type to Automatic (Delayed Start).

questions.explanation:
Registering the Azure AD Connect Health Sync agent registers the existing agent with the Microsoft Entra ID tenant and starts the Health services after successful registration. Reinstalling the agent provides another complete way to install and register it so that the server can report health data again. Service startup configuration alone does not restore a server registration that was deleted from the Connect Health list.

**Learn more:** [Install the Microsoft Entra Connect Health agents in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/how-to-connect-health-agent-install) · [Microsoft Entra Connect Health shows old information about on-premises server](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/troubleshoot/entra/entra-id/user-prov-sync/outdate-information-displays)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your on-premises network has an Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain.  
  
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You intend to implement Microsoft Entra Connect Sync and use Microsoft Entra ID Protection.  
  
You need to configure Microsoft Entra Connect Sync so that Microsoft Entra ID Protection can detect leaked credentials.  
  
What should you select?
questions.explanation:
Password Hash Synchronization transfers a securely derived password hash from on-premises AD DS to Microsoft Entra ID. Microsoft Entra ID Protection requires password hash synchronization for hybrid users to validate newly discovered leaked credentials against current tenant password hashes and generate leaked-credential detections.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra ID Protection FAQ](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-protection/id-protection-faq) · [What are risk detections? - Microsoft Entra ID Protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/id-protection/concept-identity-protection-risks)

questions.domain: Implement and manage Microsoft Entra identity and access
questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You need to add more `onmicrosoft.com` domains to the subscription. The added domains must be assignable as users' email addresses.  
  
What is the maximum number of `onmicrosoft.com` domains that the subscription can contain?
questions.explanation:
A Microsoft 365 environment is limited to a total of five `onmicrosoft.com` domains. Additional `onmicrosoft.com` domains can be created and used for user email addresses, subject to that tenant-wide maximum.\
\
**Learn more:** [Add or replace a onmicrosoft.com fallback domain in Microsoft 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/admin/setup/add-or-replace-your-onmicrosoftcom-domain?view=o365-worldwide)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 tenant.  
  
You need to create a policy that triggers an alert when unusual Microsoft Office 365 usage patterns are detected.  
  
What should you use to create this policy?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft 365 alert policies can detect unusual activity by using a baseline for normal activity and generating an alert when activity significantly exceeds that baseline. These alert policies are created and managed in the Microsoft Defender portal.\
\
**Learn more:** [Alert policies in the Microsoft Defender portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/alert-policies-defender-portal) · [Alert policies in the Microsoft Defender portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/alert-policies)

questions.domain: Deploy and manage a Microsoft 365 tenant
questions.question:
Solution: Implement password hash synchronization and change the password settings in the Active Directory Default Domain Policy.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation: Password hash synchronization enables Microsoft 365 authentication by using password hashes synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID, so authentication can continue when on-premises Active Directory is unavailable. The Default Domain Policy can enforce a minimum password length of 10 characters.

questions.domain: Deploy and manage a Microsoft 365 tenant
questions.question:
Solution: Implement password hash synchronization and change the password settings in the Active Directory Default Domain Policy.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Password hash synchronization supports cloud authentication because Microsoft Entra ID validates the synchronized password-derived hash without requiring Active Directory to be available. Microsoft Entra Password Protection enforces banned-password rules, not a configurable 10-character minimum. A minimum password length for synchronized users must be enforced by the applicable on-premises AD DS password policy.

**Learn more:** [Implement password hash synchronization with Microsoft Entra Connect Sync](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/how-to-connect-password-hash-synchronization) · [Password policy overview and frequently asked questions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/tutorial-password-policy-overview-frequently-asked-questions)

questions.domain: Implement and manage Microsoft Entra identity and access
questions.question:
Solution: Implement pass-through authentication and change the password settings in the Default Domain Policy in Active Directory.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Pass-through authentication validates user passwords directly against on-premises Active Directory. An Active Directory outage prevents that validation, so users cannot reliably authenticate to Microsoft 365 services during the outage. Although the Default Domain Policy can enforce a minimum password length of 10 characters, the authentication-availability requirement remains unmet.\
\
**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra Connect: Pass-through Authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/how-to-connect-pta) · [Troubleshoot Microsoft Entra pass-through authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/tshoot-connect-pass-through-authentication)

questions.domain: Implement and manage Microsoft Entra identity and access
questions.explanation:
Pass-through authentication validates synchronized users’ passwords directly against on-premises Active Directory, so it cannot provide authentication during an Active Directory outage. Password hash synchronization, optionally configured as a backup for pass-through authentication, is needed for cloud authentication resilience. For synchronized users, a 10-character minimum password length is enforced through the on-premises AD DS password policy; tenant password protection focuses on banned-password evaluation.

**Learn more:** [Authentication for Microsoft Entra hybrid identity solutions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/choose-ad-authn) · [Password policy overview and frequently asked questions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/tutorial-password-policy-overview-frequently-asked-questions)

questions.question:
Solution: You create an anti-malware policy.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
An anti-malware policy protects against malware but does not provide the required anti-spam and anti-phishing protections. Microsoft’s Standard preset security policy supplies a balanced baseline across anti-malware, anti-spam, and anti-phishing policies.\
\
**Learn more:** [Preset security policies in Microsoft Defender for Office 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/preset-security-policies)

questions.domain: Manage security and threats by using Microsoft Defender XDR
questions.question:
Solution: An anti-phishing policy is created.  
  
Does this meet the goal?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft’s Standard preset security policy is the balanced baseline protection profile and includes anti-spam, anti-phishing, and anti-malware protections. An anti-phishing policy alone does not provide the required baseline protection against spam and malware.\
\
**Learn more:** [Preset security policies in cloud organizations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/preset-security-policies)

questions.question:
Solution: You connect Microsoft 365 to Defender for Cloud Apps.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Defender for Cloud Apps requires at least one supported platform to be connected before OAuth app policies can be created. Microsoft 365 is a supported platform, so connecting Microsoft 365 meets that requirement.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage OAuth apps - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/manage-app-permissions) · [Create policies to control OAuth apps - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/app-permission-policy)

questions.domain: Manage compliance by using Microsoft Purview
questions.question:
Solution: You create a compliance policy.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
A Microsoft Intune compliance policy assesses device compliance, such as by using Microsoft Defender for Endpoint risk signals, but it does not onboard devices to Defender for Endpoint. Device onboarding is deployed through an Endpoint Detection and Response policy or other onboarding configuration.\
\
**Learn more:** [Configure Microsoft Defender for Endpoint with Intune and onboard devices](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-security/microsoft-defender/configure-integration) · [Onboard Windows devices to Defender for Endpoint using Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/configure-endpoints-mdm)

questions.question:
Solution: You configure Conditional Access app control.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Conditional Access app control supports Defender for Cloud Apps access and session policies that monitor and control user sessions. OAuth app policies are separate permission policies used to investigate and govern OAuth app permissions, so configuring Conditional Access app control does not enable creation of OAuth app policies. [Microsoft Learn: Control cloud apps with policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/control-cloud-apps-with-policies)\
\
**Learn more:** [Control cloud apps with policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/control-cloud-apps-with-policies) · [Create policies to control OAuth apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/app-permission-policy)

questions.question:
Solution: You configure Cloud Discovery.  
  
Does this satisfy the goal?
questions.explanation:
Creating OAuth app policies requires connecting a supported platform, including Microsoft 365, to Defender for Cloud Apps by using an app connector. Cloud Discovery provides visibility into discovered cloud apps and does not create that connection or enable OAuth app policies.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create policies to control OAuth apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/app-permission-policy) · [Manage OAuth apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/manage-app-permissions)

questions.domain: Manage security and threats by using Microsoft Defender XDR
questions.question:
Solution: Add an API token to Defender for Cloud Apps.  
  
Does this achieve the goal?
questions.explanation:
An API token only authenticates programmatic requests to the Defender for Cloud Apps API. OAuth app policies require a supported platform, such as Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, or Salesforce, to be connected to Defender for Cloud Apps; they are created from Policy management or App governance.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage OAuth apps - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/manage-app-permissions) · [Managing API tokens - Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/api-authentication)

Users access Microsoft 365 from both their laptops and a corporate Virtual Desktop Infrastructure (VDI) solution.  
  
In Azure AD Identity Protection, you enable a sign-in risk policy. Users report that, when using the VDI solution, they are regularly blocked while trying to access Microsoft 365.

For how long are alerts retained in the portal?

Add an alternate email address for User1.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Entra ID users sign in to Microsoft 365 services with their userPrincipalName (UPN). To make the required email-style identifier the sign-in name, set User1's UPN to that address; Microsoft recommends aligning the sign-in UPN with the primary SMTP address.

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You need to receive an alert when Microsoft 365 Defender identifies high-severity incidents.  
  
What should you use?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender XDR incident notification rules send email notifications for new incidents or incident updates and can be filtered by alert severity. Selecting High as the severity causes recipients to be notified of high-severity incidents.\
\
**Learn more:** [Get incident notifications by email - Microsoft Defender XDR](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/m365d-notifications-incidents)

questions.domain: Manage compliance by using Microsoft Purview
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that contains the alerts displayed in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783847621497-9m7l0yhm.png)  
  
Which alert properties can you modify?
questions.explanation:
In the Microsoft Defender/Purview portal, the only alert fields an analyst can change on an existing alert are its Status (for example Active, Investigating, Resolved) and the Comment. Severity and Category are defined by the underlying alert policy/detection and are read-only on the alert itself, so they cannot be modified after the alert is generated. This applies to both Alert1 and Alert2 regardless of their current values. Therefore only Status and Comment can be modified.

**Learn more:** [Investigate alerts in Microsoft Defender XDR](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/investigate-alerts) · [Alert policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-xdr/alert-policies)

questions.question:
You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes a user named User1.  
  
You have a Conditional Access policy applied to a cloud-based app named App1. Conditional Access App Control is deployed for App1.  
  
You need to create a Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps policy that blocks User1 from printing from App1.  
  
Which policy type should you create?
questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps session policies provide real-time control of specific activities within a Conditional Access App Control session. A session policy can use the **Printing** activity type and block it for the selected user and app.\
\
**Learn more:** [Create Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps session policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-cloud-apps/session-policy-aad)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You need to implement a passwordless authentication solution that supports these device types:  
  
- Windows  
- Android  
- iOS  
  
The solution must use the same authentication method on all devices.  
  
Which authentication method should you use?
questions.explanation:
FIDO2-compliant security keys provide a standards-based passwordless authentication method that can be used across Windows, Android, and iOS. Microsoft Authenticator passwordless phone sign-in is supported on Android and iOS, whereas Windows Hello for Business is specific to Windows.

**Learn more:** [Support passwordless authentication with FIDO2 keys in apps you develop](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/support-fido2-authentication) · [Enable passwordless sign-in with Authenticator](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory/authentication/howto-authentication-passwordless-phone)

You need to stop research-department users from accessing potentially unsafe websites through hyperlinks embedded in email messages and documents. Users in other departments must remain unrestricted.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create a data loss prevention (DLP) policy that has a Content is shared condition.
Modify the safe links policy Global settings.
Create a data loss prevention (DLP) policy that has a Content contains condition.
Create a new safe links policy.

questions.explanation:
Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Safe Links protects users when they select potentially malicious hyperlinks in email and supported Office applications. A custom Safe Links policy can be assigned to specified users or groups, allowing the research department to receive the protection without applying it to other departments. [Set up Safe Links policies in Microsoft Defender for Office 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/safe-links-policies-configure)

**Learn more:** [Set up Safe Links policies in Microsoft Defender for Office 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/safe-links-policies-configure)

Litware, Inc. is a consulting company with its main office in Montreal and a branch office in Seattle.  
  
Litware works with a third-party company named A. Datum Corporation.  
  
The Litware on-premises network contains an Active Directory domain named `litware.com`. The domain has three organizational units (OUs) named LitwareAdmins, Montreal Users, and Seattle Users, and contains the users shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783846560357-np8p1emw.png)  
  
The domain contains 2,000 Windows 10 Pro devices and 100 servers running Windows Server 2019.  
  
Litware has a pilot Microsoft 365 subscription that includes Microsoft Office 365 Enterprise E3 licenses and Azure AD Premium P2 licenses. The subscription contains a verified DNS domain named `litware.com`.  
  
Azure AD Connect is installed with the following configurations:  
  
- Password hash synchronization is enabled.  
- Synchronization is enabled only for the LitwareAdmins OU.  
  
Users have the roles shown in the following table.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783846562926-9n7r7azq.png)  
  
Self-service password reset (SSPR) is enabled. The Azure AD tenant has Security defaults enabled.  
  
Litware identifies these issues:  
  
- Admin1 cannot create conditional access policies.  
- Admin4 gets an error when trying to use SSPR.  
- Users receive new Office 365 service and feature updates before Admin2 reviews the updates.  
  
Litware plans to make the following changes:  
  
- Implement Microsoft Intune.  
- Implement Microsoft Teams.  
- Implement Microsoft Defender for Office 365.  
- Ensure users can install Office 365 apps on their devices.  
- Convert all Windows 10 Pro devices to Windows 10 Enterprise ES.  
- Configure Azure AD Connect to synchronize the Montreal Users OU and the Seattle Users OU.  
  
Litware identifies these technical requirements:  
  
- Administrators must be able to choose which version of an Office 365 desktop app is available to users and roll back to earlier versions.  
- Only Admin2 must be able to access new Office 365 service and feature updates before they are released to the company.  
- Litware users must be able to invite A. Datum users to participate in the following activities:  
  - Join Microsoft Teams channels.  
  - Join Microsoft Teams chats.  
  - Access shared files.  
- Just-in-time access to critical administrative roles must be required.  
- Microsoft 365 incidents and advisories must be reviewed monthly.  
- Office 365 service-status notifications must be sent to Admin2.  
- The principle of least privilege must be applied.  
  
You need to configure Azure AD Connect to support the planned changes for the Montreal Users and Seattle Users OUs.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: From PowerShell, run the Add-ADSyncConnectorAttributeInclusion cmdlet.
From the Microsoft Azure AD Connect wizard, select Manage federation.
From the Microsoft Azure AD Connect wizard, select Customize synchronization options.
From PowerShell, run the Start-ADSyncSyncCycle cmdlet.

questions.explanation:
Azure AD Connect OU filtering is changed by rerunning the Azure AD Connect wizard and selecting **Customize synchronization options**. This path lets an administrator choose the Active Directory domains and OUs that will be synchronized, including the Montreal Users and Seattle Users OUs.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra Connect Sync: Configure filtering](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/how-to-connect-sync-configure-filtering)

You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription and use Microsoft Defender for Office 365.  
  
You are configuring Attack simulation training that will target all users and use the Credential Harvest social-engineering technique.  
  
You need to ensure the simulation sends an email message containing a custom phishing link, along with company-specific terminology and branding.  
  
How should you configure the simulation?

A tenant payload is a custom Attack simulation training payload. lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription with Microsoft Defender for Endpoint integrated with Microsoft Intune.  
  
Devices are onboarded by using Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.  
  
You plan to block devices according to the machine risk score calculated by Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.  
  
What should you create first?

options.text: an endpoint detection and response policy

questions.explanation:
An Intune device compliance policy sets the maximum allowed Microsoft Defender for Endpoint machine risk score and marks devices that exceed it as noncompliant. Conditional Access can then block those noncompliant devices from accessing organizational resources.

**Learn more:** [Configure Microsoft Defender for Endpoint with Intune and onboard devices](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-security/microsoft-defender/configure-integration) · [Device Compliance settings for Windows in Intune](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/intune/device-security/compliance/ref-windows-settings)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.  
  
You need to create Conditional Access policies that meet these requirements:  
  
- All users must use multi-factor authentication (MFA) when signing in from outside the corporate network.  
- Users must be able to sign in from outside the corporate network only when the sign-in originates from a compliant device.  
- All users must be blocked from signing in from outside the United States and Canada.  
- Only users in the R&D department must be blocked from signing in from both Android and iOS devices.  
- Only users in the finance department must be able to sign in to an Azure AD enterprise application named App1. All other users must be blocked from signing in to App1.  
  
What is the minimum number of Conditional Access policies that you should create?
questions.explanation:
A single policy can require both MFA and a compliant device for all sign-ins outside the corporate network because Conditional Access can require all selected grant controls. Separate block policies are required for sign-ins outside the United States and Canada and for R&D users on Android or iOS, since these rules have different condition scopes. Access to App1 can be restricted with one policy that includes all users, excludes the finance department, targets App1, and blocks access. Microsoft Entra Conditional Access evaluates all applicable policies and requires all applicable grant requirements to be met before access is granted.

**Learn more:** [Build Conditional Access policies in Microsoft Entra](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-policies) · [Plan your Microsoft Entra Conditional Access deployment](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/plan-conditional-access)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Office 365 and includes a user named User1.  
  
A user sends a product catalog in PDF format to 300 vendors. Only 200 vendors receive the email, and User1 is blocked from sending email until the following day.  
  
You need to stop this issue from happening again.  
  
What should you configure?
questions.explanation:
Outbound anti-spam policies control outbound recipient limits and the action taken when a sender reaches a limit, including restricting the sender from sending mail until the following day. Configuring the appropriate outbound limits and threshold action prevents a legitimate bulk message from triggering the restriction at 200 recipients.

**Learn more:** [Configure outbound spam policies - Microsoft Defender for Office 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/outbound-spam-policies-configure) · [Outbound spam protection - Microsoft Defender for Office 365](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/outbound-spam-protection-about)

You identify a large number of recommended actions.  
  
You need to ensure that the actions can be filtered by specific department names.  
  
What should you create first?
questions.explanation:
At phishing threshold level 3 (More aggressive), Microsoft Defender for Office 365 treats messages detected with medium or high phishing confidence as very-high-confidence phishing. Consequently, messages with Medium, High, and Very high PCL values are phishing emails; a Low-PCL message is not included.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your on-premises network has an Active Directory domain.  
  
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You need to synchronize the domain with the subscription. The solution must satisfy these requirements:  
  
- On-premises Active Directory password-complexity policies must be enforced.  
- Users must be able to use self-service password reset (SSPR) in Azure AD.  
  
What should you use?

options.text: Azure AD Seamless Single Sign-On (Azure AD Seamless SSO)

questions.explanation:
The requirement that on-premises Active Directory password-complexity policies be enforced is the deciding factor. Pass-through authentication (PTA) validates every sign-in directly against on-premises AD in real time, so AD password policies, account states, and sign-in-hour restrictions are always enforced, and PTA fully supports Azure AD SSPR when password writeback is enabled. Password hash synchronization (A) authenticates in the cloud against a synchronized hash, so on-premises complexity/lockout policies are not enforced at sign-in, which is why it does not satisfy the stated requirement. Seamless SSO (C) is only a sign-in convenience feature and Identity Protection (B) is a risk-detection service, so neither performs domain synchronization or policy enforcement.

**Learn more:** [Choose the right authentication method](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/choose-ad-authn) · [Implement password hash sync](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/hybrid/connect/how-to-connect-password-hash-synchronization)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your network contains an on-premises Active Directory domain.  
  
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You implement a directory-synchronization solution that uses pass-through authentication.  
  
You configure Azure AD smart lockout as shown in the following exhibit.  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783849424407-fieghtdm.png)  
  
You discover that Active Directory users can use passwords included in the custom banned-password list.  
  
You need to ensure that banned passwords are prohibited for all users.  
  
Which three actions should you perform? Each correct answer presents part of the solution.  
  
NOTE: Each correct selection is worth one point.

options.text: From a domain controller, install the Azure AD Password Protection Proxy.
From Active Directory, modify the Default Domain Policy.
From a domain controller, install the Azure AD Application Proxy connector.
From all the domain controllers, install the Azure AD Password Protection DC Agent.
From Password protection for Windows Server Active Directory, modify the Mode setting.
From Custom banned passwords, modify the Enforce custom list setting.

questions.explanation:
On-premises Active Directory password changes are evaluated by the Microsoft Entra Password Protection DC Agent, which obtains the banned-password policy through the Password Protection Proxy. Installing the DC Agent on all domain controllers ensures every password-change request is covered. Audit mode records passwords that match the banned list but allows them; Enforced mode rejects those passwords. The custom banned-password list is already enabled.

**Learn more:** [Deploy on-premises Microsoft Entra Password Protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/howto-password-ban-bad-on-premises-deploy) · [Enable on-premises Microsoft Entra Password Protection](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/howto-password-ban-bad-on-premises-operations)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription that includes more than 2,000 guest users.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription.

Tag users and devices as honeytokens.

Microsoft Security Exposure Management uses critical assets as the targets for attack-path analysis. Attack paths might not appear or be fully representative until critical assets are defined, so critical assets must be defined before relying on attack-path visibility.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You have a data loss prevention (DLP) policy that blocks sensitive data from being shared through email messages.  
  
You need to change the policy so that, when an email containing sensitive data is sent to both internal and external recipients, delivery is prevented only for the external recipients.  
  
What should you modify?
questions.explanation:
The policy rule action controls what happens after sensitive content triggers the rule. For Exchange, the **Restrict access or encrypt the content in Microsoft 365 locations** action can be configured to **Block only people outside your organization**, allowing delivery to internal recipients while blocking external recipients.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company maintains offices in Seattle and Denver.  
  
You have a Microsoft 365 subscription.  
  
You plan to create a Conditional Access policy named Policy1 to enforce multifactor authentication (MFA).  
  
You need to ensure that Seattle office users are excluded from MFA, while Denver office users must always be prompted for MFA.  
  
What should you configure for Policy1?

options.text: a named location that has IP ranges location set to the Seattle office
a named location that has Countries location set to United States
VPN connectivity from the Seattle office

questions.explanation:
Conditional Access can use an IP-based named location to scope a policy by a user's public network address. Configure a named location containing the Seattle office’s public IP ranges and exclude that location from the MFA policy; Denver users remain in scope and are prompted for MFA.

options.text: Reset the password of User4 only.
Reset the password of any user in Azure AD.
Delete User1, User2, and User4 only.
Reset the password of User2 and User4 only.
Delete any user in Azure AD.

questions.explanation:
The User Administrator role can manage (including delete) and reset passwords for non-administrators and for members of a limited set of admin roles (Helpdesk Administrator, User Administrator, Directory Readers, etc.), but it cannot act on higher-privileged admins such as Global Administrator or Exchange Administrator. User4 has no role and User2 holds the User Administrator role, so User5 can both delete and reset the passwords of User2 and User4. User1 (Exchange Administrator) and User3 (Global Administrator) are off-limits, which eliminates "any user" (C, F) and the User1-inclusive delete option (D). Reset is not limited to User4 alone (B) because User2 is also in scope, so the two complete tasks are "Delete User2 and User4 only" (A) and "Reset the password of User2 and User4 only" (E).

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra built-in roles](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that includes a Windows 11 device named Device1 and a user named User1.  
  
User1 works from a branch office and reports slow connections to Microsoft 365 services.  
  
You need to ensure that User1 can test the connections by running the Microsoft 365 network connectivity test tool on Device1. The solution must adhere to the principle of least privilege.  
  
To which group should you add User1 for Device1?
questions.explanation:
Most tests in the Microsoft 365 network connectivity test tool require the downloadable advanced test client (MicrosoftConnectivityTest.exe), which needs the .NET 6.0 Runtime; installing that runtime requires local administrator permissions on the machine, and running the full advanced diagnostics prompts for administrator credentials. To let User1 run the tool successfully on Device1, User1 must be a member of the local Administrators group. Network Configuration Operators (B) can only change TCP/IP settings and cannot install software or run the advanced client, and Users/Power Users lack the needed rights, so Administrators is the least-privilege option that actually works.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft 365 network connectivity test tool](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/enterprise/office-365-network-mac-perf-onboarding-tool?view=o365-worldwide)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a Microsoft 365 E5 subscription that uses Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.  
  
Tamper protection is enabled in Defender for Endpoint.  
  
A device named Device1 is onboarded to Defender for Endpoint.  
  
You need to configure antivirus and real-time protection on Device1.  
  
What should you do in the Microsoft Defender portal?
questions.explanation:
Tamper protection blocks modification of protected Microsoft Defender Antivirus settings. Troubleshooting mode can be enabled for a specific device in the Microsoft Defender portal to temporarily permit configuration of antivirus and real-time protection settings.

**Learn more:** [Get started with troubleshooting mode in Microsoft Defender for Endpoint](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/enable-troubleshooting-mode) · [Manage tamper protection for your organization using Microsoft Defender XDR](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-endpoint/manage-tamper-protection-microsoft-365-defender)
